newsitem.title: UK: Willis Corroon H1 fails to lift the gloom.
newsitem.headline: Willis Corroon H1 fails to lift the gloom.

text.p: British insurance broker Willis Corroon Group Plc on Tuesday blamed intense competition and the continuing strength of the pound for a sharp fall in profits over the first six months of the year.

The decline in profits prompted analysts to revisit estimates for the full year with one suggesting that a reduction in forecasts below last year's 91.6 million pounds ($149.3 million) looked likely and that the group may struggle to make it above the 90 million pound mark.

First half pre-tax profits slipped to 60.2 million pounds, down from 68.2 million pounds while brokerage and fee revenues from continuing operations fell to 335.6 million pounds from 364.2 million pounds.

Willis again declined to comment on speculation that a tie-up with British rival Sedgwick Group could provide a solution to the problems of tough competition and slim margins, but said its plans did not include a large scale merger.

"We believe we will serve our shareholders best by following our own strategy. Certainly smaller deals are fine but we feel the risks of a major one are enormous," said Willis director of corporate communications, Peter Stevens.
Questionmarks still surround Willis' long term strategy with a widespread perception that it needs to do something dramatic to close the gap with U.S. rivals Aon and Marsh & Mclennan, analysts said.
The market gave a muted response to the figures and shares shed one penny to 126-1/2 pence by 1415 GMT.
But analysts were bearish about the immediate outlook.
"It's a horrific market. They're having to run extremely fast just to stay still and because of the currency effect they're actually going backwards," said one.
"To meet forecasts there's going to have to be a very heavy swing from first half to second."
Another analyst pointed to the accelerating competition in the U.S. between both brokers and underwriters as a particular concern and a disappointing performance in the UK energy account.
The risks, he said, were all on the downside.

Chairman John Reeve said the results were in line with expectations at the start of the year which anticipated both the acute competitive pressures, particularly in the North American and some global speciality businesses, and the unhelpful effects of the strong pound.
The latter wiped 6.6 million pounds off profits though the effects of this should moderate in the second half as comparisons ease.
For the year as a whole the group is expecting currency to reduce profits by around eight million pounds.
Competition, however, remains intense and the group hopes over time to make revenue less susceptible to insurance pricing as it increases the provision of value added advisory services.
In the short term Willis will simply have to grow the business and manage the costs as best as it can, admitted Stevens.
Reeve said the group had recently undertaken a number of initiatives to further the development of the business including the acquisition of a stake in French broker Gras Savoye.

Stevens said Willis intended to move to a majority holding in Gras Savoye over time but that the most important objective was that it retained its French character and, in all probability, a French shareholding.

The decision to place subsidiary Sovereign Marine & General Insurance in liquidation last month had a neutral impact on profits but reduced earnings because deferred tax was considered no longer recoverable.
Alongside the results Willis also announced it was establishing a joint IFA (independent financial advisory) business with Abbey National.

Full integration is expected by the end of the year and Willis said it would provide a broader range of services than either company separately and offer opportunities for more effective use of resources.
($ = 0.613 British Pounds)
